about.title: San Marino Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: San Marino is a small community, and a death here rarely stays private for long. Neighbors along Huntington Drive and Los Robles Avenue notice when a family suddenly goes quiet. In 2025 the city recorded 64 injury collisions and 91 people hurt, with no traffic fatalities in the public record that year. That is welcome news, but it does not mean wrongful death claims never arise in San Marino. Fatal losses can follow a crash on San Marino Avenue or California Boulevard, a medical error at a facility in Los Angeles County, a fall on someone else's property, or a defective product. Under California law, a spouse, domestic partner or child usually holds the first right to bring a claim, and the clock runs two years from the date of death, sooner if a public agency is involved. LawProactive does not practice law. We simply listen, then connect your family with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death matters on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why San Marino Families Reach Out Through LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, with a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first in line, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: The deadline is watched for you
items.desc: A wrongful death action in California generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting connected early keeps those dates from slipping.

items.title: Losses measured honestly
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: San Marino recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Can a wrongful death claim still exist here?
items.answer: Yes. Public collision records for San Marino show 64 injury crashes and 91 people injured in 2025 with zero traffic fatalities, but wrongful death is not limited to car crashes. A fatal fall on private property, a medication error, neglect at a care facility, or a crash that occurs just outside city limits can all give rise to a claim. Where and how the death happened will shape the case, and an attorney can review those specifics with you.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California gives the first right to a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and to the decedent's children. If none exist, the right may pass to others who would inherit under state law, and certain financially dependent relatives may also qualify. Because families are rarely simple, it helps to have an attorney confirm who has standing before proceeding.

items.question: Does a wrongful death case depend on criminal charges being filed?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death action is a civil matter brought by the family, and it proceeds separately from any criminal case the district attorney may or may not pursue. The civil case uses a different standard of proof and seeks compensation rather than punishment. A claim can move forward even if no charges are ever brought.
